source_snapshot.procedure: Green Solid when powered on; under Green Blink, no blink during BMC/HMC initialization and no blink during POST; Amber Solid/Blink not defined.
source_snapshot.criteria: Green Solid; Green Blink; Amber Solid Not Defined; Amber Blink Not Defined.
source_snapshot.script: No Script; 15 attended and 5 machine minutes.

source_snapshot.historical_v3_1: MANUAL ONLY with Source Conflict and Engineering Decision Pending; continuous phase-correlated video required, amber modes preserved undefined.

old_problem: The source expresses opposite polarities: a Green Blink section and Criteria entry imply a required blink state, while the procedure explicitly says no blink throughout both BMC/HMC and POST initialization. Sparse photos or a controller register cannot prove absence of brief optical transitions, and Amber Solid/Blink have no acceptance definition.
disposition_reason: Retain Pending and Source Conflict, not BLOCKED. ED-09/ED-08 settle the method: a qualified operator must capture uninterrupted contextual/close visual evidence and any register is corroboration only. However no general rule can choose between actual Green Blink and prohibited blink without falsifying one source statement. Engineering must provide a revision-scoped phase/state matrix and amber disposition before final PASS.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX row 1912, same-row DeepSeek/test-json, GPT V2, historical record, pending/conflict analyses and ED-01 through ED-30 were read. The next formal locked-queue identity was directly opened as Functionality row 1913 / Wistron-HW-00463-V002 / 0f400c1ce90bf42b.
ED-09 requires true human visual evidence for a physical LED; ED-08 similarly prevents controller state from substituting for emitted color/cadence.
Continuous video aligned to BMC/HMC and POST phase markers is required because still images can miss short transitions at ownership handoffs.
The Green Blink label/criterion and two no-blink instructions are irreconcilable without an authoritative polarity decision; choosing either would manufacture PASS semantics.
ED-13/ED-15 prohibit treating undefined amber modes as N/A or PASS without platform specification and criteria.
No power-on, reset, LED stimulus, physical observation, register read, retry or DUT action was performed.

test_case.test_name: Power Button LED power-on and initialization behavior — pending polarity decision
test_case.purpose: Visually verify the exact Power Button LED from an approved power-on event through BMC/HMC initialization, POST and stable powered state, preserving both the solid-green requirement and the unresolved Green Blink/no-blink polarity plus undefined amber states.
required_package: Exact physical Power Button LED and controller mapping plus hardware/BMC/HMC/BIOS revision
Approved phase/state matrix resolving Green Blink versus no-blink for BMC/HMC, POST and steady state
Observable phase markers, maximum timing and defined color/cadence/duty-cycle tolerance
Revision-scoped Amber Solid/Blink definitions or specification-backed N/A disposition
Approved power-on stimulus, continuous contextual/close video, passive telemetry and independent recovery
test_case.test_command: MANUAL ONLY; after the phase/state matrix and power-on authorization are approved, a qualified operator records one uninterrupted contextual and close video of the exact Power Button LED from before the power-on event through BMC/HMC initialization, POST completion and stable powered state. Correlate every visible transition to console/BMC/HMC/power timestamps and any approved read-only controller state. Do not use a register as optical proof, invent amber fault stimuli, reset/power-cycle outside the approved sequence or automatically retry.
test_case.expected_result: Green is solid at the approved powered-on stable point. Initialization behavior cannot receive final PASS until Engineering decides whether blink is required or prohibited in each BMC/HMC and POST phase and supplies cadence/timing limits. Amber modes are evaluated only when defined or specification-backed N/A. No unexpected color/cadence, boot stall, power instability or platform fault occurs.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: Current review remains Pending because polarity and amber acceptance are unresolved. After approval, PASS requires uninterrupted video proving every phase/state/timing criterion and clean platform health. FAIL on wrong color, unauthorized blink/no-blink, cadence/timing violation, missed phase, evidence gap, BMC/HMC/POST stall or power/thermal fault. A controller bit, sparse snapshots or assumed amber N/A cannot PASS; end user owns verdict.
safety_gate: Do not issue any power/reset stimulus without explicit approval and independent recovery.
Use direct continuous visual evidence; a register or SSH status is supporting-only.
Do not invent amber stimuli or acceptance and do not resolve the Green polarity by reviewer preference.
Stop on stalled POST, BMC/HMC loss, power instability, thermal/fault indication or evidence loss; no automatic retry.
expected_evidence: Approved indicator mapping, platform revisions and phase/state/polarity/cadence/timing matrix
Continuous timestamped contextual and close video through power-on, BMC/HMC, POST and stable state
Synchronized console, BMC/HMC phase, passive power and any supporting controller-state evidence
Amber state or specification-backed N/A disposition
Power authorization, abort/no-retry/recovery audit and engineer/end-user verdict
test_case.recovery: If boot, power, thermal or indicator behavior is abnormal, stop observation, preserve continuous evidence and do not retry. Use the independently approved platform recovery to return to the defined stable state; any further reset or power cycle requires a new explicit authorization.

source_conflict.reason: Green Blink is named as a section and criterion while the instructions prohibit blinking in both initialization phases; no approved polarity decision exists.

blocked.reason: The manual observation method and evidence can be prepared; final acceptance remains Pending on the phase/state decision rather than being technically impossible.
